//: The modules that PRESENT a credential and DECLARE no scopes. Read by scripts/derive-grants.mjs. Each entry names a FILE, not a service, so it cannot quietly widen into a service's whole grant the way the old hand-maintained compose map did. An entry whose module has since grown an exported *_SCOPES constant is STALE and FAILS the derivation, so this file shrinks as the repositories that own these modules do the work — it cannot be padded. A reason under 40 characters fails, the same rule service-ci.yml applies to scope-exemptions.json. NONE OF THESE ARE MICRO-DEPLOY'S TO FIX; each names the repository that owns it.
// three deleted, and the ratchet is wha: market/src/policyclient.ts, wallet/src/custodyclient.ts and wallet/src/settlement.ts were removed once micro-market and micro-wallet declared their own outbound scopes: POLICY_SCOPES is now policy:decide, CUSTODY_SCOPES is custody:address:create, and SETTLEMENT_SCOPES exists at all for the first time. derive-grants --check FAILED on all three before the deletion and passed after with the compose block BYTE-IDENTICAL, which is the proof the entries were stale rather than merely deletable: the repositories derived exactly the scopes micro-deploy had been supplying by hand, and nothing was lost with them.
// and the three empty ones went too, th: An empty declaration used to be indistinguishable from no declaration — both parsed to zero scopes, so a module whose upstream needs nothing could not say so and failed the build instead. derive-grants.mjs reads `export const FOO_SCOPES = Object.freeze([])`, and its named form `NO_SCOPES_REQUIRED`, as the verdict it is: cleanly declared, no entry needed, no scope granted. The three entries that carried `"scopes": []` are now gone, because the repositories that own those modules said it themselves — devplatform/src/membership.ts exports IDENTITY_SCOPES = Object.freeze([]) (contracts-auth is not a dependency there and taking one on for an empty constant would put a package in the image for no runtime effect, the call indexer/src/rpc.ts already made), mint/src/index.ts exports RPC_SCOPES = NO_SCOPES_REQUIRED, foresight/src/proposer.ts exports PROPOSER_SCOPES = NO_SCOPES_REQUIRED. derive-grants --check FAILED on all three as stale before this deletion — naming each constant and its line — and passes after with the compose block BYTE-IDENTICAL, which is the proof the same thing is now said once, by the module that knows it, instead of twice.
// what is still owed, and it is not a d: wallet/src/pricingclient.ts and trade/src/pricingclient.ts have never had entries here: both declare PRICING_SCOPES = pricing:read cleanly, and both headers say in as many words that the declaration is WIDER than the call site needs, kept only because an empty one used to be unsayable. The one route either client calls is GET /rates (pricing/src/server.ts:312), which pricing does not gate — READ_SCOPE guards :422 and nothing else those clients touch. Narrowing both to NO_SCOPES_REQUIRED is right and is AD-05, but unlike the three above it is NOT byte-identical here: it removes pricing:read from the trade and wallet grants, so it needs `node scripts/derive-grants.mjs --write` against docker-compose.estate.yml in the SAME window as the two repositories declare, or --check goes red in whichever direction lands first. That regeneration is micro-deploy's, and it has not been done.

admin-api/src/upstreams.ts.reason: micro-admin-api owns this. Its header carries a full route-and-guard table but no exported constant. The scopes are read off that table: this service's own service token is used for LEDGER ALONE — GET /trial-balance and GET /accounts/:subject/balances (ledger:read), POST /entries and POST /entries/:id/reverse (ledger:post) — because ledger's authorise() refuses a user principal outright. It also needs identity:admin for PUT /internal/users/:id/roles (admin-api/src/upstreams.ts:464, identity/src/server.ts:1584), the route the identity.role.grant executor calls and the path by which EVERY administrator after the first is promoted; admin-api/src/actions.ts:116 names this as still owed by micro-deploy. Its market and billing calls deliberately forward THE OPERATOR'S OWN BEARER so those services record which administrator acted (SD-11), which is why market:read, market:admin and billing:read are absent here despite being in the old hand-written compose map: no service token ever carried them.

tessera/src/studioclient.ts.reason: micro-tessera owns this. Two call sites, two scopes, and they are deliberately not collapsed into the wider one: POST /v1/generations (tessera/src/studioclient.ts:93) is gated on WRITE_SCOPE = studio:write (studio/src/server.ts:420), and the poll that follows it — GET /v1/jobs/:id, 'the status URL a 202 points at' (studio/src/server.ts:472) — is gated on READ_SCOPE = studio:read. A generation is a REAL CHARGE against studio's credit ledger, which holds real USD (studio/src/credits.ts:43), so the write scope is the expensive half and the polling half must not silently inherit it. Reported to micro-tessera; delete this entry when it exports STUDIO_SCOPES.

tessera/src/marketclient.ts.reason: micro-tessera owns this. It builds a token-bearing HttpClient and it is NOT a service-token client: every write relays THE PLAYER'S OWN bearer — `input.sellerToken`, tessera/src/marketclient.ts:108, 'The SELLER's bearer token, relayed. Never a service credential' — and the one read, GET /v1/listings/:id, sends no authorization at all. Its header states the reason rather than assuming it: the token the player presented to Tessera is already a token market accepts, so relaying it grants market exactly the authority the player has and not one scope more. An empty list is the derivation, not a placeholder; granting market:write here would hand tessera a credential able to list on any player's behalf, which is the shape SD-05 retired. Delete this entry the day micro-tessera exports MARKET_SCOPES = NO_SCOPES_REQUIRED, which is now expressible.

tessera/src/communityclient.ts.reason: micro-tessera owns this. Same shape as its market client and for a stronger reason: community REFUSES a service token on the founding route — its own comment at tessera/src/communityclient.ts:31-34 quotes the gate, 'A service token is not close enough on the governance surface. It names no user', throwing ForbiddenError. So POST /v1/communities carries `input.founderToken`, the founding admin's own bearer, relayed. There is no scope that would help: a wider grant here would be a credential that still cannot make the call. Ward governance is one member one vote (23-tessera.md §7.1's second refusal) and a service principal has no membership to vote with. Delete this entry when micro-tessera exports COMMUNITY_SCOPES = NO_SCOPES_REQUIRED.

billing/src/ledger.ts.reason: micro-billing owns this. It builds a token-bearing HttpClient for ledger and exports no scope constant, unlike billing/src/adminapi.ts in the same repository which does. Derived by reading its two call sites: POST /entries (ledger/src/server.ts:346) and POST /entries/:id/reverse (:394), both gated on POST_SCOPE = ledger:post. It reaches no other ledger route, so ledger:read and ledger:reserve — which the old hand-written compose map granted it — were never used by anything and are dropped here.

custody/src/policy.ts.reason: micro-custody owns this. It posts to policy's POST /v1/decisions (custody/src/policy.ts:70) with a token-bearing client and declares no constant. custody had NO entry at all in the hand-written compose map, so this scope has never been grantable and every policy decision custody asked for would have been refused the moment it was wired up — a defect the derivation found rather than the four agents who hit grant failures by hand.

worlds/src/titleclient.ts.reason: micro-worlds owns this. It is the provisioning bridge and the reason it declares no constant is structural rather than an oversight: its base URL is per registered title, resolved at runtime from worlds' own registry, so there is no single named peer to hang a FOO_SCOPES constant on — the grant is therefore ONE SCOPE PER TITLE THAT CAN BE PROVISIONED, and it grows with the estate rather than with this file's age. It calls POST /v1/provision, gated on PROVISION_SCOPE = aetherholm:provision (aetherholm/src/server.ts:130, 400) and on tessera:provision (tessera/src/server.ts:330, = PROVISION_SCOPE at tessera/src/scopes.ts:39); its other call, GET /v1/title, is deliberately public on both. tessera:provision is what finally gives the world.private.small SKU a code path — it has existed in billing since billing/src/migrations.ts:405 and no title has ever served it. The registry states both scopes are held by worlds alone, and estate-verify drives the tessera one end to end rather than asserting it, which the aetherholm one cannot be because that service has no container here.
